questions: Should the normalization be applied per column (feature) across all rows (samples) as StandardScaler does by default, or should it be applied differently (e.g., per row, per entire array)?
After reshaping, what should be the order of dimensions in the flattened result? Should it be C-order (row-major) or F-order (column-major)?
What should happen if the inputs contain NaN or infinite values? Should the function raise an error, propagate them, or handle them somehow?
Should the StandardScaler be fitted on the entire result array, or should it be fitted and transformed per batch or dimension?
What should the DataFrame index be? Should it be default RangeIndex, or something else (e.g., based on input dimensions)?
If the multiplication result has zero variance in some columns, how should StandardScaler handle it? Should it scale to zero, leave as is, or raise an error?
Should the function accept inputs of any numeric dtype (e.g., int, float32, float64) and convert them, or require a specific dtype?
What is the exact error message format for incompatible shapes? Should it include both shapes fully or just the mismatched dimensions?
